summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease, and a history of chronic abdominal pain was admitted for sharp, stabbing right lower quadrant abdominal pain, bloating, and nausea. Initial CT with oral contrast showed no obstruction, but the patient later developed fever and leukocytosis. A follow-up CT with IV contrast revealed a right kidney lower pole infarct. Subsequent renal ultrasound with Doppler confirmed absent blood flow in the affected area. Transesophageal echocardiogram showed complex atheroma in the aortic arch and a small plaque near the left main coronary artery, suggesting a possible embolic source. The patient improved with pain management and an aggressive bowel regimen. She was started on low-dose aspirin and simvastatin, with plans to follow up on pending hypercoagulability tests and cardiology evaluation. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her prednisone taper and monitor for warning signs.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
